readiness.mainReason: The switch is the right shape of answer but the saving it rests on is stated with no build, so the client would be deciding on a number it cannot defend.
readiness.highestRiskIssue: Slide 9 states a 2.4 million euro saving with no build and no source, and slide 13 recommends the switch on the strength of it.
readiness.whatCouldChangeIt: The build behind the saving, unit prices and volumes with their sources, would settle this and could move it to Nearly ready.

blockingIssues.label: Headline saving is ungrounded and the recommendation depends on it

evidence.quote: Switching supplier delivers a 2.4 million euro saving.

strengths.point: The option set is defined on the axes a client would actually use.
strengths.quote: Three suppliers were compared on unit price, lead time and recycled content.

findings.title: The recommendation rests on a 2.4 million euro saving that is stated with no build behind it and no source.
findings.principle: Evidence grounding: the number a decision turns on carries its own build.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 9 states the saving as a finished figure. No slide shows the unit price delta, the volume it is applied to, or where either input comes from. Slide 10 gives a direction of travel, not a build.

evidence.quote: Switching supplier delivers a 2.4 million euro saving.
The saving comes from a lower unit price and fewer part loads.

findings.why: The client cannot defend the figure to its board, and if the build is wrong the whole switch is wrong. This is the finding that sets readiness.
findings.reflect: Write the saving as an equation. Which input are you least able to source today?
findings.fix: Show the build behind the saving and name the source of each input, or state it as a range with the assumptions it depends on.

findings.title: The rollout goes straight to full migration without the pilot the switch would normally earn.
findings.principle: Implementation: a reversible first step de-risks an irreversible one.
findings.diagnosis: Slide 14 sets a two quarter window from switch to complete migration with no staged step in between.

evidence.quote: Begin the switch in Q1 and complete migration by Q3.

findings.why: If Supplier B underdelivers on lead time the co-operative has already moved every depot.
findings.reflect: What would you need to see in the first quarter to be sure the switch is working?
findings.fix: Stage the rollout so one region proves the unit price and lead time before the rest follow.

findings.title: Slides 11 and 12 carry the same chart title, so a reader cannot tell what changed between them.
findings.principle: Slide titles carry the argument, not the label.
findings.diagnosis: Two consecutive slides are titled identically with no action title distinguishing them.
findings.why: A skimming reader reads the pair as a duplicate and stops looking for the difference.
findings.reflect: What does each of these two slides prove that the other does not?
findings.fix: Give each slide the action title that states its own point.

comments.problem: The revenue figure sits alone with no link to the packaging line.
comments.why: A reader cannot size the saving against the business without it.
comments.fix: Put the packaging spend beside the revenue so the saving has a denominator.

questionsForLead: Has anyone checked the unit price quote behind the saving with the supplier directly?

learningNote.lesson: The number the recommendation turns on is the one that has to be built up in front of the client.
learningNote.weakHabit: Presenting a computed figure as a finished fact.
learningNote.exercise: Take the headline number and write it as an equation with a source beside every input.

notAssessed: The supplier quotes themselves were not seen, so the unit price could not be verified.
Slides 6 and 7 are image only in the extract and were not assessed.
